prompt: I bought a battered old record cover, and I (to surprise) to find a 1969 ticket inside.
explanation_ru: Здесь surprised — прилагательное, описывающее состояние (был удивлён), а не действие.

prompt: The lower bed on that Vietnamese night bus simply (not / to fit) my long legs.

prompt: Your diving mask (to need / adjust) before the boat leaves at six-fifteen tomorrow morning.
explanation_ru: Конструкция need + -ing имеет пассивное значение и равна need to be + V3.

prompt: We were at eight-all in the fifth squash game when the court lights suddenly (to go) out.
explanation_ru: Свет погас сам по себе (went out) — непереходный глагол, пассив здесь невозможен.

prompt: My nine-year-old son (to bear) in Madrid, and he just lost his first tooth biting an apple.
explanation_ru: Выражение «родиться» в английском всегда используется в пассиве в Past Simple: was born.

prompt: Does that old iron pan in Oslo (to need / clean) before you cook?
explanation_ru: После need для пассивного значения используется герундий (need cleaning) или to be + V3 (need to be cleaned).

prompt: Before every game, the playing field (to need / clean) and marking with white lines.
explanation_ru: Поле нуждается в уборке: needs cleaning (need + -ing передаёт пассивный смысл).

prompt: A bright green tie never (to suit) a weather presenter standing in front of a green screen.
explanation_ru: Глагол suit (быть к лицу, подходить) не употребляется в пассиве.

prompt: Why (not / old drawings / to display) in the sunny gallery? Because daylight damages the paper.
explanation_ru: Отрицательный вопрос в Present Simple Passive описывает постоянное правило хранения гравюр.

prompt: When a tray of tools arrives from the operating room, it (to need / clean) with hot steam immediately.
explanation_ru: Конструкция need + -ing (needs cleaning) передаёт пассивный смысл: поднос нужно очистить.

prompt: I felt so sorry for the grocery robot that (to stick) behind a parked van on my pavement.
explanation_ru: Здесь stuck выступает как прилагательное состояния (застрявший), а не действие.

prompt: Nobody in our Bath book club had finished the novel, so we (not / to bore) — we just ate cheese.

prompt: Each painted canvas backdrop in the Newcastle fly-tower (to weigh) ninety kilos, yet one technician can lift it.
explanation_ru: Глагол weigh в значении «иметь вес» является глаголом состояния и не используется в пассиве.

prompt: Old silk flags (not / to wash) easily, so experts use a fine mist through a net.
explanation_ru: Активная форма с пассивным значением (ergative verb): «не стираются легко» — do not wash easily.

prompt: Modern lead (to lack) the radioactive purity required for the underground cosmic-ray detector in Yorkshire.
explanation_ru: Глагол lack (не хватать, не иметь) никогда не употребляется в пассивном залоге.

prompt: My grandfather, who (to bear) during the war, would have loved the ration books we found under the floorboards.

prompt: Our client meeting on the fourteenth floor was going fine. Suddenly, a window cleaner's platform (to drop) right past the glass. We (to amuse) when the cleaner held up a sign scoring our slides nine out of ten.

prompt: Our cat vanished in Toronto yesterday, and my daughter (to worry) sick. We searched the whole street in the rain. Eventually, we noticed that the airing cupboard door (not / to shut) properly, and we found him fast asleep inside.

prompt: The harbour's chain-ferry looks simple, but it is clever engineering. Two heavy iron chains (to lie) on the bottom all day. When the ferry crosses, the chains (to lift) over drive wheels and dropped back into the water.

prompt: I had a bizarre morning on the Underground. The magnet in my saucer rim (to wake) my e-reader screen up inside my bag. Before I knew it, three expensive thrillers (to buy) automatically!
explanation_ru: Магнит сам разбудил экран (актив). Книги были куплены (пассив, действие завершилось до того, как он заметил).

prompt: Every morning this week, ripe tomatoes (to disappear) from our Devon garden. My husband was convinced birds were to blame. Then our toddler walked in with red juice on his shirt — the mystery (to solve)!
explanation_ru: Глагол disappear непереходный, он никогда не ставится в пассив. Загадка оказалась разгаданной (was solved).

prompt: Brand-new linen shirts look far too clean for a Shakespearean battle scene. They (to need / age) before filming starts. First, they are rubbed with earth, and then they (to drag) round the gravel car park until they look six months worn.

prompt: Deep inside a Svalbard mountain, foil packets of wild wheat seeds are stored at minus eighteen degrees. Even if the electricity fails, the seeds (to stay) completely frozen. That is because the surrounding permafrost (not / to need / cool) artificially.

accepted_answers: does not need to be cooled

prompt: A tiny library (to appear) inside an old Sheffield bus shelter last month. Nobody knows who built the shelves, yet the paperbacks (to change) every day. Commuters say the shelter no longer feels gloomy.
explanation_ru: Appear — непереходный глагол (пассив невозможен). Books read well — активная форма с пассивным значением («хорошо читаются»).

prompt: At my friend's party, the new cream sofa ___ cleaning after someone spilled red wine on it.
explanation_ru: Конструкция need + -ing (needed cleaning) имеет пассивное значение, сам глагол need стоит в активе.

prompt: A giant inflatable duck ___ on a Milton Keynes roundabout overnight, and nobody has claimed it.
explanation_ru: Глагол appear непереходный — он никогда не используется в пассивном залоге.

prompt: The first wild beavers ___ in that Scottish forest in four hundred years are already building dams.
explanation_ru: Причастие born (рождённые) используется в определении без вспомогательного глагола.

prompt: Hong Kong double-decker buses ___ a windscreen transponder that pays the harbour tunnel toll automatically.
explanation_ru: Глагол have в значении обладания не имеет пассивной формы.

prompt: In that Cardiff pharmacy, the automated picking robot ___ any human help to find the right carton.

explanation_ru: Глагол resemble (напоминать, быть похожим) — глагол состояния, он не употребляется в пассиве и Continuous.

prompt: Six pinned beetles collected in Java in 1860 ___ tiny mites still preserved under their wing-cases.

prompt: My 2008 hatchback passed the brakes test, so I ___ when it failed over a pair of fluffy dice.

prompt: During the night race in Dalarna, runners are not worried about getting lost in the wet forest.

answer: Insulated silicone domes cost very little, yet they keep hospital soup hot for forty minutes.

prompt: During a Diwali party in Leicester, all the lights in the street went off, but hundreds of small lamps were already shining along the road. Which sentence describes the state of the lamps?

explanation_ru: Were lit описывает уже существующее состояние (лампы горели / были зажжены), а не процесс зажигания (were being lit).

prompt: At Borough Market, aged Comté cheese is very popular and customers buy it very fast. Which sentence uses an active form with a passive meaning?

prompt: A guest left one riding boot in a Bath hotel in November. The reception supervisor sees it in the cupboard and notices it is covered in mud. What does she say?

prompt: In a Dresden computer factory, small silicon discs travel in airtight boxes. No dust can enter them because the lids stay tightly shut. Which sentence is natural and correct?

prompt: On Lake Constance, the orchestra sits indoors while the stage floats outside. The musicians are watching the conductor on six screens right now. Which sentence describes the state of the stage?
